prompt:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: A displacement-time graph for a walker moving along an east-west path. East is defined as the positive direction.
Stage 1 (0 to 20 s): straight line from (0 s, 0 m) to (20 s, 60 m).
Stage 2 (20 to 35 s): horizontal line at s = 60 m.
Stage 3 (35 to 50 s): straight line from (35 s, 60 m) to (50 s, 0 m).]
(a) Determine the velocity of the walker during the first 20 s. [1]
(b) State the velocity of the walker between t = 20 s and t = 35 s. [1]
(c) Calculate the velocity of the walker between t = 35 s and t = 50 s. [1]
hints: In part (a), calculate gradient Delta s / Delta t for the first stage.
In part (b), the line is horizontal.
In part (c), the walker returns to s = 0; find Delta s = 0 - 60 and divide by Delta t = 15 s.
teacher_walkthrough: Stage 3: gradient = (0 - 60) / (50 - 35) = -60 / 15 = -4.0 m s^-1. Negative sign indicates westward motion.
